Subject: Clarification: region pinning, snapshots, and key destruction

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of gating questions before we finalize the Dedicated contract:

1) Non-replication: We need explicit confirmation that when we pin our Dedicated deployment to us-west-2, no customer data (storage volumes, snapshots, caching artifacts, or telemetry) will be replicated to any other AWS region or cloud provider.

2) Snapshots & backups: Are snapshots taken at the region only? If backups exist, where are they stored, how long are they retained, and can we require them to be disabled or set to a strict TTL?

3) Key custody & destruction: We require evidence that cryptographic keys used to encrypt customer data can be destroyed (or rendered unrecoverable) on request and that any HSM-backed keys leave no recoverable material. We also need the attestation language you can sign.

4) Proof of deletion: For regulated data, we need a procedural document that describes how you demonstrate an in-place wipe versus relying on logical deletion (e.g., manifests, checksums, snapshot IDs, wipe runbooks).

Can you point me to the artifacts you can provide (redacted if needed), and a timeline for delivery? Procurement would like an attestation they can attach to the SOW.

Best,
Asha

Thanks — good, specific questions. Below is a high-level summary and a list of artifacts we can deliver. I've also looped in our infra and security leads (aditya, karthik) for detail.

Summary commitments (high-level):
- Region pinning: For Redwood Dedicated, when you request pinning to a region (e.g., us-west-2), we allocate tenant-scoped resources in that region and do not replicate customer data to other AWS regions or third-party clouds as part of normal operation.
- Snapshots/backups: Automated snapshots are region-local by default; cross-region replication is not enabled for tenant snapshots unless explicitly requested. Retention is configurable per-customer.
- Key custody & destruction: We use HSM-backed keys for production encryption. We can provide key identifiers and HSM attestation, and we support a documented key destruction workflow (redaction and verified zeroization) that can be triggered by request.
- Proof-of-deletion: We will provide a wipe playbook, snapshot manifests (IDs/checksums), and a signed attestation template.

Deliverables we will provide by 2028-04-18 EOD:
1) redwood_nonrep_commitment.pdf (PDF attestation language + infrastructure description)
2) snapshot_policy_diagram.png (diagram showing region-local snapshots and retention)
3) kms_key_serials.csv (redacted key IDs and HSM cert thumbprints)
4) a wiped-data manifest template you can attach to your audit.

If the attestation language needs legal redlines, we can circulate a DocuSign-ready statement. Would you like us to prepare the DocuSign now or wait for redlines?

I'll follow up with the attachments.

Irene / team — quick technical notes we can share:

1) Region pinning and replication model
- For Dedicated (pinned) tenants we provision tenant-scoped EBS volumes, local NVMe instance caches, and S3 buckets (if used) inside the pinned region
- Cross-region replication is not enabled by default at any tier (EBS, S3, or internal object stores).

2) Snapshots/backups
- Snapshots are EBS snapshots in the pinned region and use AES-256 encryption with HSM-wrapped keys. We can toggle automated snapshot schedules per-tenant.
- Default retention: 7 days; configurable to a minimum of 0 days (i.e., no automated snapshots) or extended as requested.
- Snapshot manifest: we can export a CSV with snapshot_id, creation_timestamp, volume_id (redacted), checksum (sha256), and retention_until. See attached example (snapshot_policy_diagram.png used for architecture, and we can produce a manifest).

3) Telemetry & metrics
- Lightweight telemetry (service metrics) is aggregated to a central control plane, but payloads do not contain tenant-level payloads or raw input/output content. We can route telemetry for specific enterprise customers to a VPC endpoint in the same region where required.

4) Snapshots & backups not replicated
- We confirm there is no automated cross-region replication for tenant snapshots unless specifically enabled via an explicit customer request and a change ticket.

I'll prepare the snapshot manifest and attach redacted examples.

— Aditya
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Team — security notes for the attestation and artifact bundle:

1) KMS/HSM
- Production encryption uses HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3 certified HSMs in our cloud provider fleet). We do not export raw key material. We can provide key identifiers (key_id) and HSM attestation certificates (thumbprints) as part of the package.
- Key destruction: HSM vendors support zeroization; our KMS provider will mark keys as schedule_for_deletion, then execute a vendor-backed zeroize operation. We can commit to initiating destruction on request and provide the HSM zeroize certificate (vendor-generated).

2) Attestation language (recommended)
- Proposed short clause: "Redwood Inference attests that, for the pinned Dedicated deployment described in this document, customer data will not be replicated outside the specified region except where explicitly requested by the customer; cryptographic keys used to encrypt customer data are managed in HSMs and can be zeroized on customer request subject to mutually agreed operational controls."
- Legal can review, but this is concise and audit-friendly.

3) Proof-of-wipe artifacts
- We will provide: wipe runbook excerpt (sanitized), sanitized audit logs showing operation timestamps and operator IDs, snapshot manifests (IDs + checksums), and HSM zeroize receipts where applicable.

Note on timelines: generating vendor HSM zeroize certificates requires coordination with the KMS vendor (48–72 hours). We should flag that to the customer.

— Karthik
Head of Security & Compliance
